correctness.rationale: The exact Gaussian transition diagonalizes every centered quadratic mode; Cauchy--Schwarz reduces worst-case autocorrelation to the largest cosine-square expectation. A Fejer-square nonnegativity lower bound is attained by the uniform nontrivial roots-of-unity times at mean pi/2. Equality forces the Fejer zero set, Fourier inversion determines symmetric masses, and antisymmetric mean constraint yields the complete family. Verified code executes exact-rational budgets and 339 deterministic spectral/Fejer check groups; no finite test substitutes for the all-K proof.

originality.rationale: New assessed scientific statement is the sharp fixed-mean iid-duration HMC minimax for all centered quadratic observables and classification of all equality laws; closest primary papers use random finite time grids for mixing bounds, squared-statistic adaptive heuristics, deterministic Chebyshev schedules, or exponential timing laws. The Fejer kernel identity itself is classical. The inspected published claims and available prior scientific records did not imply this theorem; unindexed historical overlap is an explicit residual risk.
residual_risks: The Fejer moment bound is classical; an unindexed spectral design/HMC theorem could already state the full result in equivalent language.
No independent survey of all historical HMC or extremal trigonometric probability literature has been completed.
Other objective functions, nonquadratic HMC observables, general frequencies and cost-normalized numerical integrators are not covered.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly solves a motivated expected-integration-length-budget design problem for HMC covariance-estimation efficiency across all quadratic observables, yields exact finite-dimensional performance (3K-1)/(K+1), classifies all designs, and identifies a nontrivial uniqueness transition from K=3 to K=4. For K>=2 the deterministic duration at the same mean leaves a quadratic frequency resonant forever, making the finite randomized optimum substantive. Scope is deliberately limited to exact ideal HMC and arithmetic frequency spectra.
